summary: Preserve atom identity and sourced bond events across frames without guessing reaction chemistry from distance.
objective: Build a reactive-trajectory inspector where explicit atom mapping and per-frame bond events show which bonds form or break, with provenance visible at every frame.
intent_signals: reaction breaks and forms bonds across trajectory frames
inspect explicit bond events without distance inference
example_prompts: Show a short supplied reaction trajectory with stable atom IDs and explicit bond add/remove events, then reject an unmapped frame.
negative_signals: Not a bond-perception heuristic, reaction-path calculation, force field, mechanism proof or rate prediction.
not_for: No bond inference from distance, changing atom identity, missing event provenance, molecular dynamics integration, electronic structure or causal mechanism claim.

entities.name: Mapped atoms and bonds
entities.guidance: Blender supplies atom sockets and bond-segment families. Three.js retains atom ID across frames, reuses objects by ID and changes bond objects only from validated topology events.

entities.name: Frame provenance ledger
entities.guidance: Pin source frame, time/unit if supplied, atom-map status and ordered add/remove/change events beside before/after topology. XYZ is admitted only as coordinates plus an explicit sidecar contract.

state_contract.model: Finite ordered frames. Each frame has unique stable atom IDs, element labels and finite Cartesian coordinates with declared length unit; atom-set changes are out of scope. Initial topology is an explicit set of unordered atom-ID pairs with declared bond label/order provenance. Each later frame carries an ordered atomic event batch add/remove/change(old,new); validate referenced IDs, prior existence/absence and duplicate conflicts before committing the complete batch. Coordinates may come from XYZ, but ID mapping and topology must come from a separate provenance-bound manifest; line order alone is never silently treated as identity after mismatch.
state_contract.authority: Three.js owns IDs, frame index, topology events, validation and snapshots. Blender owns reusable atom/bond presentation meshes and never guesses connectivity.
actions: Load an initial mapped frame and explicit topology, then validate all frames before playback.
Step one frame and inspect the atomic before/event/after topology diff.
Select a bond to see the exact source event that created, removed or changed it.
Reject missing/duplicate IDs, contradictory events, unknown endpoints or coordinate-only topology requests; reset returns frame zero.

invariants: Every frame contains each declared atom ID exactly once with unchanged element label; a mismatch stops playback before mutation.
Topology changes only through the current frame’s validated event batch; geometric distance may be displayed but never creates a bond.
Applying a valid batch then its exact inverse restores the preceding topology; rejected batches preserve prior state.
A bond event is an annotation from the supplied source/model, not evidence that the visualization discovered a mechanism.
motion_guidance: Step commits one source frame or declared transformation; pause preserves committed state and reset restores data, view, selections and errors.
Offer a static frame/table alternative. Tweened atom, curve or surface motion explains correspondence only and never creates scientific samples.
creative_affordances: Blender may establish a distinctive molecular stage, lattice frame and stable atom/orbital glyph families; Three.js binds them to scientific IDs and data.
Materials, camera and composition remain flexible when units, provenance, sign, identity and uncertainty stay legible without color alone.
known_limits: Fixed atom set and supplied event provenance only; no claim that topology labels are experimentally correct or that sampled frames resolve an elementary mechanism.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no chemistry calculation, trajectory conversion, Blender export, browser, renderer or interactive artifact was run.

physical_contract.scope: Scientific coordinates and annotations drive display; mesh contact and animation do not compute chemistry.

object_craft.structure: Use stable keyed atom cores, replaceable bond sleeves and a fixed before/after event rail; topology changes should remain visible when animation is paused.
object_craft.material: Encode element and bond-event status with label, pattern and outline as well as color; distinguish sourced bonds from optional distance guides.

claims.statement: The generic XYZ format described by Open Babel consists of atom count, a comment line and element symbols with Cartesian coordinates; multiple frames can occur, but the page describes no stable atom identifier or explicit bond list in those core lines.
claims.scope: Open Babel XYZ coordinate representation only; this recipe therefore requires a separate explicit ID/topology manifest rather than treating XYZ as reactive connectivity.

source_refs.locator: Format description and lines 1–11: atom count, comment, element and Cartesian-coordinate fields, multiple frames
